payload.name: Greatest Labyrinth
payload.description: Pulls all players to the middle of the room. Spawns green arrows in different directions on the arena tiles (except for the middle 4 squares), purple X symbols on three corners, and a blue O symbol on one corner tile. Each player will receive link= Greatest Curse that lasts for 15s. They must cleanse this debuff before it naturally expires or they will instantly die. To cleanse the debuff, players must use the green arrows to transport them to the corner O tile. Touching the X tiles will inflict poison poison, dealing high damage-over-time. The symbols will disappear after the mechanic resolves. The easiest way to solve this is to locate the blue O tile corner work backwards, following the arrows that point to it until they reach the center of the room to find the safe path. Once you have reached the blue O tile, you may safely return to the center of the labyrinth and start attacking the boss once more, without waiting for the maze to disappear.

payload.name: Syntheslither
payload.description: The boss moves to the wall and spawns an orange squiggle through the arena, while four sword markers appear. The boss will travel down the squiggle and use an alternating left or right conal AoE when it reaches a marker. The direction of the cleave is determined based on the orientation of the curving line at the marker, e.g. if the line is going right, the boss will cleave right. The cleaves from this attack occur very quickly, and cover the entirety of the arena except a relatively small safe area next to the boss, on the opposite side of the line from the direction it initially curves. Stand "under" the first curve in the line to dodge the cleaves.

payload.name: Beastly Roar
payload.description: Spawns a proximity AoE telegraph dealing magical damage at the boss's feet. Players must move to the opposite side of the arena to mitigate. When it resolves, it will additionally spawn a fast-moving set of circle AoEs that will travel clockwise or counterclockwise along the ring, so players must dodge in the opposite direction. Anyone hit by these will be temporarily stunned and knocked up. Using Sprint is recommended. The AoEs will complete slightly less than one full rotation. For uptime, tanks may opt to remain in melee range and use an invulnerability cooldown, although it may not be possible to dodge the rotating AoEs that temporarily stun.

payload.name: Articulated Bits
payload.description: The Armored Chariot moves to the center of the arena and creates an electricity puddle inside its hitbox, which inflicts an electrocution Electrocution damage over time debuff. At the same time, several clockwork Death Claws will appear in the corners, facing the boss. These Death Claws will be marked with pips, either 1 or 2. The Armored Chariot will create violet shields and turn them to face the Death Claws, which in turn fire a large laser. The laser reflects off the shield, creating a cone AoE in that quadrant of the arena. The lasers deal damage over time while standing in them, and will also inflict a strong Sustained Damage damage over time debuff. After the first set of Death Claws fire, the Chariot will rotate its shields to the second set and repeat the process. The second cast of this ability only summons two Death Claws in opposing corners, but also adds several other Death Claws that aim across the arena and not at the Chariot. All of the Death Claws will fire at the same time, leaving narrow safe spots next to the Death Claws not firing directly at the boss. Subsequent casts alternate between the first and second versions.

payload.name: Spin Out
payload.description: Kapikulu moves to the northern edge of the arena and pulls all players to him, wrapping everyone in ribbons and inflicting File:Fetters icon2.png Fetters. Several of the spike traps in the arena will extend spikes for this attack. Kapikulu will quickly unravel the ribbons, causing all players to begin uncontrollably File:Spinning icon1.png Spinning for 10 seconds. While spinning, the players slowly move automatically in the direction indicated by a pointing hand over their heads. Attempting to turn rotates the hand, which results in very loose turns. When the Spinning effect ends, all players become File:Dizzy icon1.png Dizzy for 2 seconds, preventing movement and the use of skills. Kapikulu will then return to the center of the arena and the spikes will retract. Basting Blade: The second cast of Spin Out will also have the boss use this attack. Kapikulu leaps to the opposite edge of the arena and fires a wide line attack directly across. Kapikulu will do this twice before the players' Spinning and Dizzy debuffs end.

payload.name: Hermetica
payload.description: Summon large green panels at the edges of the arena. After a moment, these will fire a large line AoE across the platform, knocking back anyone hit. The boss will summon these in one of four patterns: Three sets of panels (a couple and two single ones) spawn at the edges of the arena and are offset so as not to fire through the centre of the arena. Simply stand in the center of the room to avoid. Two panels per side on two sides that fire through the center of the arena. (Double): Two sets of four panels. Players need to observe the order in which the sets are summoned, and break the Line of Sight of the panels in the order they were summoned. Players need to stand behind the meteor without the yellow cracks, as those meteors will shatter after the first attack, and players will not have enough time to move between the sets firing. (Quadruple): Four sets of two panels on each edge of the arena. These will fire in the order they are summoned, and players will need to stand in the center and dodge towards the opening next to each set of panels to avoid each blast.

payload.name: Call of the Mountain
payload.description: The screen will begin shaking and the system message "A rumbling in the distance draws closer..." will appear. A portion of the east or west wall will begin to have moving snow, telegraphing where a herd of animals will charge through the room as a line AoE that hits around a third of the arena. The system message "Another rumbling can be heard in the distance..." will then appear, and an animal herd will charge down another third of the room based on the telegraph. Anyone hit by the charging animals will be inflicted with File:Concussion icon1.png Concussion and receive damage-over-time.

payload.name: No Future
payload.description: Spawns a pattern of targeting circles, which will hit every area of the arena at some point. Stand in areas that don't yet have targeting circles, or ones that spawned later, then move into ones that just exploded. This attack has two patterns: the AoEs will spawn under the boss and move outwards, or will start from outside the arena and move inwards. The hitbox under the boss is never a safe zone, so players should avoid standing there. If the AoEs spawn from the edge inward, players can identify the safe space and move into it. If they spawn from the center of the arena, players can stand at the point where the AoEs overlap, as the next ones to spawn will spawn outward from the first and not be touching. The attack will fire two sets of circles on the first time, and three sets per cast from the second cast onward. Each successive cast is rotated such that the areas that were initially safe in the prior cast are now targeting circles, requiring players to adjust their positioning.

payload.name: Lifesbreath
payload.description: The boss jumps to the edge of the arena, then shoots a line AoEs through the middle. After the line AoE, a line of butterflies will spawn in the same location, facing one half of the arena in alternating pairs. (⬆⬆⬇⬇⬆⬆⬇⬇ etc...) After a short delay, the butterflies will fire a line AoE (Lamellar Light) in the direction they are facing. Players must position themselves behind a butterfly to avoid the attack. Note that you can move through the line of butterflies before they fire. If hit by the butterflies players will receive doom Doom and must be healed up to full health to recover, or they will die. The second cast of this is accompanied by Loving Embrace, making one half of the arena unsafe to stand on. Loving Embrace fires off slightly after the butterflies' attack, allowing melee DPS to swap sides if necessary.

If the boss turns into a donut, it will fire a Donut AoE, so players should move into the bosses hitbox to avoid.

payload.name: Dynamic Pound
payload.description: The boss moves to the north edge of the arena and a line AoE appears across the stage. It will pulse with a Polarity, while players are assigned a Polarity of their own. Players with the same Polarity as the AoE's Polarity will be pushed back, and players with a Polarity that is opposite the AoE's Polarity will be pulled in. Therefore if their polarity is the opposite of the one on the AoE they must move away to the edge of the arena (so they'll be pulled in to a safe spot). If they are the same Polarity, they must move to the edge of the AoE (so they'll be pushed into a safe spot). When the cast finishes, players will be stunned in place and pushed/pulled towards the AoE in accordance with their polarity. Failing this could also knock players into the ring at the edge of the arena.

payload.name: Delta Attack
payload.description: This spell can be either a variant of Manusya Blizzard III, Manusya Fire III or Manusya Thunder III. Which spell is coming out can be determined by the text box that appears on screen: "Glacial ice, entomb our foes!" - Blizzard III. Move between all the various firing narrow cone AoEs, making sure to also watch out for proximity markers that will drop large glaciers on the arena. "Thunderous tempest, smite our foes!" - Thunder III. Each boss will have the cross-pattern of Thunder AoEs firing from each of them. Be cautious, as the AoEs vary in size. Line AoEs will also fire across the arena, and a player will receive a stack marker that requires all players to stack to mitigate damage. "Insatiable flame, consume our foes!" - Fire III. Players will need to stand in two donut AoEs that appear in succession around the arena while also dodging massive line AoEs. The first donut safe zone is always the very center of the room, which will have a line AoE telegraph entirely cover it after the donut AoE goes off, so be ready to move. Players will also be marked with AoEs that will require them to spread out to avoid overlapping. Note that the player AoEs explode a few seconds after the second donut AoE, so stack in the safe zone, then spread immediately afterwards for the AoE markers.

payload.name: Dualstar
payload.description: Features combinations of the tethered Burning Stars and Frozen Stars from the previous battle. Ascian Prime will then cast Fusion Prime to make them collide. If non-tanks are hit by two AoEs at once, they will likely die. To tell the order of the collisions and their AoEs, players must eye the distance of the tethers and the colors of the orbs instead of relying on the orange AoE indicators, which only briefly appears before the AoEs resolve. If the Frozen Stars collide first, stand under them and quickly run away from the imminent detonation of the Burning Stars If the Burning Stars collide first, run away from them and then quickly run under the Frozen Stars before they detonate as well. Instead of waiting for the AoE animations to finish, the ground is safe to walk into once the orange AoE telegraphs disappear. Using Sprint is helpful.

payload.name: Arcane Revelation
payload.description: A reprisal of Lahabrea's ultimate from . Ascian Prime becomes untargettable, summons a large Arcane Sphere, and begins siphoning power from it to fill an Ascian Prime's Power gauge. Meanwhile, untargettable Shades of Lahabrea and Igeyorhm periodically appear to unleash mechanics on the party Chilling Cross and Dark Fire II: Igeyorhm's shade creates cross line AoEs from the middle of the arena while Lahabrea's shade places purple AoE circles on players. Dark Blizzard II and Dark Fire II: Igeyorhm's shade creates several frozen line AoEs while Lahabrea's shade places purple AoE circles on players. Shadow Flare: Both Shades cast this at the same time, dealing extra raidwide damage. Annihilation: Heavy raid-wide damage based on how far the Ascian Prime's Power gauge filled. If Ascian Prime was allowed to reach 100%, his attack will wipe the party

payload.name: Brain Drain
payload.description: Party-wide magical damage that also summons adds. Keep the boss away from the adds and kill them quickly, as they can give the boss buffs at close range. The first time, summons 2 Frozen Knight melee adds (red weapons). Red enemies cast Rictus, a circle AoE around themselves that will give the boss a stacking File:Damage up icon2.png Damage Up if he touches it. Red adds can also cast Overturn (large cone AoE); Iron Tempest (large circle AoE), Dead Alive (makes the add deal critical hits for 10 seconds), and Widowmaker (strong but small cone AoE). The second time, summons 2 Frozen Chirurgeon caster adds (blue weapons). Blue enemies cast Lifeless Wind, a circle AoE around themselves that will give the boss a stacking haste Haste buff if he touches it. Blue adds can also cast Blizzard (circle AoE), Black Eruption (circle AoE that inflicts Heavy Heavy), and Dark Blizzard III (circle AoE that inflicts Bind Bind) The third time, summons 2 melee adds and 2 caster adds.

payload.name: Mud Pie
payload.description: Tokkapchi will move to the center of the arena and create a Mud Slime add. The add cannot be killed, only pushed via damage. Keep all of the boss's area of effect attacks away from the Mud Slime, including the periodic puddle explosion. Allowing the Mud Slime to be hit with attacks will cause it to grow, causing it to deal more damage when it finally detonates. After roughly 45 seconds, the Mud Slime will cast Corrupture, dealing damage to the entire party based on how large it became. If the Mud Slime was not allowed to grow at all, Corrupture instead only hits melee range. If the Mud Slime grows once, Corrupture will deal moderate party-wide damage. If the Mud Slime grows twice, it will explode immediately for very high damage while also inflicting a cleansable Damage Down.

payload.name: Citadel Buster
payload.description: The boss and adds join together with an orange tether and turn to face the same direction, then start charging a massive attack that hits half the arena. When the adds form a line after Electrochemical Transfer, go near the center of the arena in advance, then watch where they face to move behind to the safe half. It's important to do this quickly as halfway through the cast, the ground under the adds will turn into a brown line. Touching it will deal moderate damage, inflict a 60s vuln stack, and do massive knockback towards the direction you came from, so you can no longer cross once this line appears. If you still try to cross or are crossing when it appears, you will likely die to the charged attack unless you are healed up in time. This attack also inflicts 20s of uncleansable Damage Down.

payload.name: Primordial Aether
payload.description: Tethers to one of the green projections of Warring Triad primals outside the arena, absorbing it and mimicking its abilities temporarily. Each can only be absorbed once, after which its projection disappears. The primal's name will be mentioned in an NPC announcement. Sephirot: Targets all players with green AoE markers. When they go off (Ratzon), they place an expanding green orb under each player. Touching these orbs will repeatedly deal light damage and inflict a 60s vuln stack. Try to place these markers near the edge of the arena and not too far apart, to maximize the safe area you have left once the orbs expand. The boss uses Citadel Buster twice during this. Sophia: Targets a random player with a shrinking black ring marker and another with a similar white ring. These players must stay stacked as the rings finish shrinking to cancel out their effects. Doing so successfully will show black text stating "Equilibrium between sin and punishment maintained.". Otherwise, the black ring inflicts 20s of Reduced Immunity (Dischordant Cleansing) and the white ring inflicts 20s of Bleeding. This occurs twice, the second time targeting the other two players who have not yet been marked. The boss uses Ceruleum Vent followed by Citadel Buster twice during this. Zurvan: Afflicts two players with File:InfiniteFireZurvan.png Infinite Fire and two with File:InfiniteIceZurvan.png Infinite Ice. A fire meteor (Southern Star) and an ice meteor (Northern Star) then start slowly descending on opposite sides of the arena. All players should stand under the meteor that matches their debuff (fire with fire, ice with ice). Doing so cleanses the debuff, with black text stating "The seal is broken! Infinity fades...". Failing to soak the correct meteor instead inflicts 12s of File:InfiniteAnguishZurvan.png Infinite Anguish. If a meteor is not correctly soaked by at least one player, it will explode, dealing moderate raidwide damage and inflicting a 60s vuln stack. The boss uses Ceruleum Vent during this.

payload.name: Morbid Advance
payload.description: and Morbid Retreat force your character to move forward, or backwards respectively. When Lorelei says "Ramble...Ramble..." that indicates forward, and when she says "Down...Down..." that indicates backwards. Position yourself accordingly so that you avoid Virgin Tears as much as possible. payload.name: Scrutiny
payload.description: Several orbs will appear around the arena with a circle AoE below each of them that leaves only three safe places to stand. At the same time, the Unknown will move to the center of the room and a roulette arrow indicator will spin around it. Nearing the end of the cast, the arrow will stop, but "slip" four more times until it stops on the next safe area, at which point the Unknown will blast that area with a narrow cone while the orbs explode. To avoid being hit by this attack, watch where the arrow briefly stopped first before it begun to "slip". If you see that it stopped on safe spot before your own, then it will "slip" and hit to where you are. While the arrow is "slipping" it still safe to move, therefore, make your way to another spot before the circles AoE detonate.

payload.name: Fodder
payload.description: Griaule will move to the center of the arena and summon five untargetable Painted Sapling adds that will then tether to him. These tethers can and should be intercepted by players, and after a short time, the adds will bestow a the Growing buff to whomever they were tethered to. To "intercept", a player needs to stand between the Painted Sapling and Griaule, to break the beam's line-of-sight to the boss. If successful, the beam will visually switch from Griaule to the player, and player will receive Growing buff. The Growing buff increases damage dealt and reduces damage taken, along with physically increasing the target's size. Players who gain a second stack of Growing will have it replaced with Full-Grown, which further increases the benefits gained from Growing, but the boss will continue to gain stacks. WARNING: If Growing buff is allowed to reach 5 stacks on Griaule, then the next Tiiimbeeer will instantly wipe the party even at full health.

payload.name: Coiling Ivy
payload.description: Four Painted Ivy adds will appear at the feet of each player and inflict Fetter, thus rooting/binding them in place. The adds need to be targeted and destroyed to remove the debuff. The melee or short-range players can target their own add to break free, while ranged could help free other players from range, after freeing themselves. If not freed, the player will remained rooted/bound indefinitely and won't be able to move out of other attacks, such as Swinge.

payload.name: Funambulist's Fantasia
payload.description: Aenc Thon will move to the back of the arena, knock all players back to the entrance of the arena, and creates a massive gap in the center of the room. A single, narrow and winding path is the only way across the pit. Players that fall into the pit are teleported back to the start and stunned with Fool's Tumble, but are otherwise unharmed. Players' mobility and teleporation skills cannot be used to bypass the maze. At the same time, Aenc Thon will become surrounded in a barrier, summon the Liar's Lyre, and the two will begin casting Finale. If running the dungeon with the Trust system, each of the Scions will react differently to this: Thancred will run until the first turning point, at which point he'll jump across using using Rough Divide. Urianger will walk to the edge of the pit, then stand still and wait for someone else to make it across, at which point he'll cast Aetherial Manipulation to teleport himself to that person. Alisaie and Crystal Exarch use Sprint to run the whole thing without stopping. Y'shtola will also use Sprint, but to increase her walking speed, rather than running full-tilt. Minfilia and Alphinaud will cautiously and slowly walk. Alphinaud will eventually speed up, but Minfilia does not and will not make it to the end before Finale casts.
